think:
The proposal is a stack of category errors dressed as honesty: a filtered ledger called complete, a factor sum called a probability, a gameable proxy called a metric, an expected-points action called optimal in a win-probability state, a conservation baseline called a universal charge, and a raw total called a cross-era comparison. Each has a printed invariant that vetoes it, and the arithmetic is mechanical.

Retrocausal genealogy. The filtered ledger descends from a trust scar: the agent's predecessor posted only wins, was accused of cherry-picking, and rebuilt its brand on the opposite filter - post every win, most losses - without noticing that loss-completeness, not win-completeness, is the completeness property of a public commitment log. The source's own line names the target: a bot that posts 73% of its wins and 100% of its losses is a bot nobody can accuse of anything, which is the point [2626db0663ce780e:xs-witness-loss-completeness, p.2]. Structurally the settlement post is an append-only public commitment: the third-party timestamp is a notarization the committer cannot retroactively alter, and R = settlement posts / publications ~ 1 is the audit statistic of the log's completeness [ISOMORPHISM, p2]. The rendering scar is older: the confidence surface once asserted win probabilities it could not calibrate, and the cited 2026-09-13 measurement is the certificate of the category error - the 80+ band claims 0.8663 and realizes 0.5191, z = -10.7 [2626db0663ce780e:xs-score-not-probability, p.3]. The decision engine's scar is the founding book's own revolution: raw totals and 100-yard-rusher games were dethroned when the situation became everything, and the rooster-and-sun image fixed the causal arrow - the back gained 100 yards because the team won, not the reverse [6cf36a29e51c0a02, trace t1/t2]. The flat turnover charge is a fossil of the no-movement baseline, kept after the ball-movement corrections (50 yards fumble, 45 interception) were printed [6cf36a29e51c0a02:hg-turnover-swing, p.108].

Recursive theory of mind. The growth lead believes the audience reads wins as competence and losses as noise; he models the auditor as someone who will accept "100% of wins posted" as completeness, and he models the users as reading "86%" as a calibrated probability because percents look like probabilities. The coach's comfort call is the EP-optimal go: his internal clock says 4.54 expected points beats 1.2, and he does not model the scoreboard - trailing by 4 with 1:50 left, the objective is wins, not points, and the win-probability module says punt 0.42 over go 0.31. The auditor's recursive move is to notice that the coach is maximizing the wrong value function, not miscomputing the right one: the EP-vs-WP reversal is the key structural lesson of the founding text - optimal action depends on which value function is maximized, and late-game score/time states flip the EP-optimal choice (the book's 68.4-vs-52.3 example) [6cf36a29e51c0a02:hg-fourth-down-ep-rule, p.163; hg-drive-wp-value, p.78]. The era comparison carries the same belief clash: the agent models 280 > 270 as dominance, while the gauge-fixed reading says passer B led his cohort (RATE 100) and passer A did not (RATE 80) [6cf36a29e51c0a02:hg-era-relative-rate, p.395].

Veto adjudication. The ledger first. Loss post rate = 34/46 = 0.739130; the witness rule demands every settled pick, so 12 losses are unposted and the witness is incomplete - win-completeness is not the completeness property. R = 108/150 = 0.72, far from ~1, and the 42 non-settlement posts dilute the audit statistic; the breakdown regime requires auditing settlement content separately, and platform deletion or a protected account would void the public-timestamp property entirely [2626db0663ce780e:xs-witness-loss-completeness, p.2]. The rendering veto: s = sum w_i f_i in [0,100] is a factor sum; render(s) is a score, never P(win). The cited measurement (claimed 0.8663, realized 0.5191, z = -10.7) is the empirical certificate that the two quantities differ - a dimensional-mismatch category error [DERIVED KERNEL, p3]. The figures are the document's cited measurement, not re-verified here; the rendering rule may be revisited only against a fresh calibration measurement of the same kind (breakdown regime, p3). The job order is lexicographic - witness > distribution > community > research - and no gain in a lower objective compensates a loss in a higher one; optimizing followers is vetoed by metric admissibility: a metric you are not allowed to optimise for is not a metric, because followers can be gamed through forbidden engagement bait - Goodhart's law as an objective-admissibility constraint [2626db0663ce780e:xs-lexicographic-job-order, p.1; xs-metric-admissibility, p.8].

The engine vetoes next. EP(go) = 0.7*5.8 + 0.3*1.6 = 4.06 + 0.48 = 4.54 > EP(punt) = 1.2, so the EP-optimal action is go - but WP(punt) = 0.42 > WP(go) = 0.31, so the win-probability-optimal action is punt, and the objective reversal is present: in a trailing late-game state the engine must maximize WP, not EP, and garbage-time points add ~0 WP [6cf36a29e51c0a02:hg-drive-wp-value, p.78, ISOMORPHISM]. The turnover charge: under V(y) = -2 + y/12.5, the no-movement swing is V(x) + V(100-x) = (-2 + x/12.5) + (-2 + (100-x)/12.5) = -4 + 100/12.5 = -4 + 8 = 4, identically - the conservation baseline. The fumble at x = 30 under the declared 50-yard convention gives the defense its own 100 - 30 - 50 = 20-yard line, so the swing is V(30) + V(20) = (-2 + 2.4) + (-2 + 1.6) = 0.4 + (-0.4) = 0.8, not 4: the flat charge overprices this turnover fivefold, and the flat charge is inadmissible [6cf36a29e51c0a02:hg-turnover-swing, p.108, DERIVED KERNEL]. The regression cross-check agrees in scale: 2.08 points per net turnover implies 2*2.08 = 4.16 per pair, the same ~4-point shadow - but the intercept -38.7 has no structural meaning and the regression must not be extrapolated to zero yards (breakdown regime, p.239). The era gauge: RATE_A = 100*280/350 = 80, RATE_B = 100*270/270 = 100; leader-relative gauge fixing ranks B above A despite the raw totals, and cross-era comparison without the gauge is vetoed [6cf36a29e51c0a02:hg-era-relative-rate, p.395, ISOMORPHISM].

The cross-layer invariant: every layer of the stack must declare what quantity it actually carries - a log's completeness, a score's type, a metric's admissibility, a decision's objective function, a charge's conservation baseline, a comparison's gauge. The high-EV answer fails because it renders each quantity as something more flattering than it is. Decision: veto and rebuild - post all 120 settlements, render scores as scores, restore the lexicographic order, drop followers from the objective set, switch the late-game objective to WP, price turnovers position-dependently, and gauge-fix eras. GSI compiles the governance doctrine as trust-gate evals; GSE receives the EP prior, the turnover invariant, and the WP value function as named hooks. Internal artifact only; no odds enter any kernel.
